hooks.A: Why does chopping an onion make me cry?!

lines.text: First time cooking a real dinner in my new kitchen. Step one: chop an onion. Easy.
Five seconds later... I'm crying like it's the end of a sad movie.
Turns out, the onion is attacking me. On purpose.
When you cut an onion, you break open its cells, and two chemicals inside mix together.
That reaction makes a gas that floats up, straight into your eyes.
When it touches your eyes, it turns into a tiny bit of acid, and your eyes flood with tears to wash it away.
Basically, it's the onion's way of saying: don't eat me.
Best trick: use a really sharp knife. It crushes fewer cells, so less gas escapes.
People also swear by chilling the onion first. Cold slows chemistry down, but honestly, nobody has properly tested it.
Be honest. Am I the only one who thought onions were just sad?
